newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-GREENE READY TO CHALLENGE WORLD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-GREENE READY TO CHALLENGE WORLD.

text.p: Newly-crowned U.S. 100-meter champion Maurice Greene has a warning for the world's elite sprinters: watch out.
"It's time for an American to step up," Greene said Friday after winning the U.S. title in 9.90 seconds to equal the 10th fastest time ever run.
Americans have not won a championship 100-meter title since Carl Lewis's 1991 world title. Canadian Donovan Bailey holds the world record at 9.84 seconds.
"I think it's time for someone to stand up, and I'll do that to help put American sprinting back where it's supposed to be," Greene said/
"I have a strong feeling the American foursome will be the one winning gold," he said of the 400-meter relay at the world championships.
That, too, would be a tall order. Olympic champion Canada has won the last two major championships' sprint relays.
